narrative.overview:
Paste is a near-black reading instrument. Every surface is one of three paper tiers, separated by 1px hairlines rather than by shadow, and every number the machine produced — an id, a hash, a byte count, an expiry date, a line number — is set in a mono face so a reader can tell at a glance which words came from the product and which came from a person. The system was established in the project's approved dark-only prototype and has held across twelve milestones; src/app/globals.css is its single source of truth and there is no light theme to maintain.

The register is forensic rather than dramatic. Panes are quiet (--paper-2 on --paper), code sits on a recessed --paper-3 band, and colour appears only where it carries meaning: amber where something is live, red where something is refused, green where something is clean, blue where something is a machine-read figure worth noticing. There are no gradients used as surface fill, no glass, no elevation shadows, and no decorative imagery — this product renders text, and the rules the prototype carried for photographic treatment were dropped on the way in.

Density is high and deliberately tabular. The recurring unit across every screen is a definition list of hairline-divided fact rows — label left in muted ink, machine value right in mono with tabular figures — used by the expiry readout, the 410 tombstone, the save receipt, the retention table and the home page's figure rail. That row is the house pattern; a new surface that needs to state facts should reach for it before inventing anything.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, three paper tiers, hairline --rule dividers at 1px
Two semantic accents: amber for live, red for refusal (plus green for clean, blue for figures)
Host Grotesk for language, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for machine-written values only
10px radius on nearly everything; flat surfaces, no elevation shadows
4px spacing grid; a 1440px measured column with a 64/24/16px gutter
Motion is scoped, information-bearing, and absent by default

rules.name: The Two Accents Rule
rules.body: Amber owns live and affirmative state; red owns refusal. They are not interchangeable and neither is ever used as decoration. A new surface that wants a colour for "important" does not get one.

rules.name: The Live-State Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the thing that is currently true — the loaded tab, the selected lines, the session, the primary action. If a device would be amber in two places on one screen for two different reasons, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Machine-Written Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for values the machine produced. It is never a costume for making prose look technical — if a human wrote the words, they are set in Host Grotesk.

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Any figure that is compared down a column carries the num utility (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums): sizes, line counts, view counts, dates.

rules.name: The Measured Column Rule
rules.body: Every route renders inside container-page. AppShell's bleed prop is the single documented exception, for a surface that composes its own full-width regions; it drops the container and its padding and that surface then owns its own gutters.

rules.name: The Hairline Grid Rule
rules.body: Regions are divided by a 1px --rule border on the shared edge, not by a gap, a background change or a card. A fact table is a dl of rows each carrying border-b border-rule, with the last row's border removed.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast. If a region needs to read as separate, change its paper tier or give it a hairline. The only box-shadow anywhere in the build is a 2px inset brand band used as an underline on the loaded sample tab, which is a border substitute and not a licence to introduce elevation.

rules.name: The Earned Motion Rule
rules.body: An animation ships only if it carries information: the consequence of a choice, the arrival of a refusal, the exit of a row from a queue. Default is no motion.

rules.name: The One Gesture Rule
rules.body: One event gets one moving object. Two things moving to announce one save reads as a product pleased with itself.

rules.name: The Quoted Control Rule
rules.body: When a real component is embedded in an argument as evidence, it keeps its shape and loses its fill: the region is inert, and descendant buttons and links are stripped to a --rule border with --ink-2 text, so a quoted primary action cannot compete with the page's own.

dos: Do take every colour, radius, type step and duration from src/app/globals.css. It is the single source of truth, declared through Tailwind v4 @theme / @utility.
Do keep the two accents semantic: --brand for live and affirmative, --bad (with --bad-soft) for refusal, --ok for clean, --cool for a notable machine figure.
Do set every machine-written value in --font-outlier, with num on anything compared down a column.
Do build fact statements as hairline dl rows — label left in muted ink, value right in mono.
Do divide regions with a 1px --rule border and a change of paper tier.
Do wrap routes in container-page; use AppShell's bleed only for a surface that composes its own full-width regions.
Do give every loading placeholder role="status" with an aria-label, shaped like the thing it replaces.
Do keep the view route to its single client module (body-tools.tsx) and its transitions in CSS; view-page-budget.spec.ts and view-route-imports.spec.ts fail the build otherwise.

Do keep stored render output free of inline style attributes — Shiki declarations are moved to generated classes by src/lib/render/tokens.ts so the per-request-nonce CSP can stay at style-src 'self' (asserted by no-inline-styles.spec.ts).
donts: Don't add an elevation shadow, a glass/backdrop-blur surface, or a gradient used as a surface fill. (Gradients as a mask-image overflow fade are an existing, legitimate device; the prohibition is on gradients as decoration.)
Don't add a light theme or a .dark class. The system is dark-only and :root carries the palette.
Don't render a refusal in amber or a live state in red.
Don't use mono as a technical costume for prose, or proportional figures in a column.
Don't declare --spacing-* theme tokens; that namespace also drives sizing utilities and will silently collapse max-w-*.
Don't introduce a motion token outside the 90-200 ms ease-out band, or a spring on anything containing text. The 900 ms save receipt is the only carve-out and it is already documented.
Don't animate the view page or the 410 tombstone, and don't add an entrance or scroll-reveal animation to the home page.
Don't put more than one amber-filled primary action in a region, and don't leave a quoted component's primary fill intact.
Don't invent customers, logos, testimonials, counts or traffic figures as visual content; PRODUCT.md records that none exist.
